sections.title: Identification
sections.text: A milkcap with a 3–8 cm cap, initially convex and slightly depressed at the centre, becoming more deeply depressed with age. The smooth cap is a little sticky in damp weather and distinctly zoned: brown-orange to greyish pink or lilac-grey, with darker zones and sometimes greenish marks. The pale orange gills are moderately crowded and slightly decurrent; they may turn green when bruised. The cylindrical stem, 4–8 cm tall (occasionally 11 cm) and 1–2.5 cm wide, is pinkish buff to dull brown-orange, usually without distinct pits; it may turn green where damaged. Flesh is pale in the centre and orange beneath the cap skin and above the gills; the stem becomes hollow with age. Latex is scanty and orange, slowly reddening, then sometimes turning green and grey as it dries on the flesh.

sections.title: Habitat and range
sections.text: An ectomycorrhizal species associated mainly with spruce (Picea), in boreal and mixed forests. It is documented in Sweden and Finland, with summer-to-autumn records; in Estonia, records remain difficult to separate from Lactarius deterrimus. Alpine reports exist, but some collections resembling L. fennoscandicus have been reassigned to L. deterrimus after molecular examination. Ecology and locality help interpret a collection but are not sufficient to identify it.

sections.title: Similar species and food status
sections.text: Lactarius deterrimus is a close lookalike that is also associated with Picea: its cap tends to be brighter orange and less distinctly zoned, and its stem more uniformly orange. In L. fennoscandicus the cap is generally darker, brown-orange to lilac-grey and strongly zoned, while the stem is duller. Intermediate forms are frequent; reliable determination may require a fresh specimen, its host tree, latex colour change and microscopic characters. The Finnish Food Authority includes L. fennoscandicus in its list of mushrooms recommended as food. This listing does not validate a photographed collection: eat only a confidently identified specimen and follow local preparation guidance.

traits: Brown-orange to greyish pink or lilac-grey cap, distinctly zoned, 3–8 cm wide and becoming more depressed at the centre
Pale orange, moderately crowded, slightly decurrent gills that may turn green when bruised
Dull pinkish-buff to brown-orange stem, usually without visible pits; scanty orange latex slowly becomes reddish
Ectomycorrhizal with spruce, especially in boreal forests of Sweden and Finland
Close to Lactarius deterrimus; intermediate forms can make identification difficult
safetyNote: L. fennoscandicus is included in the Finnish Food Authority's list of mushrooms recommended as food. Milkcaps in section Deliciosi are similar and can be confused; this image and entry cannot validate a collection. Eat only specimens identified with certainty and follow local preparation guidance.
